# `SelectionDAG` Class

<p>This is used to represent a portion of an LLVM function in a low-level Data <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/dependence">Dependence</a> DAG representation suitable for instruction selection. <a href="#details">More...</a></p>

## Description {#details}

<p>This is used to represent a portion of an LLVM function in a low-level Data <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/dependence">Dependence</a> DAG representation suitable for instruction selection.</p>


<p>This DAG is constructed as the first step of instruction selection in order to allow implementation of machine specific optimizations and code simplifications.</p>


<p>The representation used by the <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/selectiondag">SelectionDAG</a> is a target-independent representation, which has some similarities to the GCC RTL representation, but is significantly more simple, powerful, and is a graph form instead of a linear form.</p>


<p>Definition at line 228 of file <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/include/include/llvm/include/llvm/codegen/selectiondag-h">SelectionDAG.h</a>.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Create a <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/constantfpsdnode">ConstantFPSDNode</a> wrapping a constant value.</p>


<p>If VT is a vector type, the constant is splatted into a BUILD_VECTOR.</p>


<p>If only legal types can be produced, this does the necessary transformations (e.g., if the vector element type is illegal). The forms that take a double should only be used for simple constants that can be exactly represented in VT. No checks are made.</p>

### computeKnownBits() {#a0138c9b735258330db2232fb84b368bf}

<div class="doxyMemberItem">
<div class="doxyMemberProto">
<table class="doxyMemberLabels">
<tr class="doxyMemberLabels">
<td class="doxyMemberLabelsLeft">
<table class="doxyMemberName">
<tr>
<td class="doxyMemberName">KnownBits SelectionDAG::computeKnownBits (<a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/sdvalue">SDValue</a> Op, <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/lib/lib/target/lib/target/aarch64/aarch64promoteconstant-cpp/#a90f8350fecae261c25be85d38b451bff">const</a> <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/apint">APInt</a> &amp; DemandedElts, unsigned Depth=0)</td>

</td>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Determine which bits of <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/namespaces/llvm/#ab471937b9a227e70c7fe8bd9604014d6">Op</a> are known to be either zero or one and return them in Known.</p>


<p>The DemandedElts argument allows us to only collect the known bits that are shared by the requested vector elements. Targets can implement the computeKnownBitsForTargetNode method in the <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/targetlowering">TargetLowering</a> class to allow target nodes to be understood.</p>


<p>The DemandedElts argument allows us to only collect the known bits that are shared by the requested vector elements.</p>

### ComputeNumSignBits() {#ac01c66c983bfbac05a0cf903f08417df}

<div class="doxyMemberItem">
<div class="doxyMemberProto">
<table class="doxyMemberLabels">
<tr class="doxyMemberLabels">
<td class="doxyMemberLabelsLeft">
<table class="doxyMemberName">
<tr>
<td class="doxyMemberName">unsigned SelectionDAG::ComputeNumSignBits (<a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/sdvalue">SDValue</a> Op, unsigned Depth=0)</td>
</tr>
</table>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Return the number of times the sign bit of the register is replicated into the other bits.</p>


<p>We know that at least 1 bit is always equal to the sign bit (itself), but other cases can give us information. For example, immediately after an "SRA X, 2", we know that the top 3 bits are all equal to each other, so we return 3. Targets can implement the ComputeNumSignBitsForTarget method in the <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/targetlowering">TargetLowering</a> class to allow target nodes to be understood.</p>


<p>Declaration at line 2056 of file <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/include/include/llvm/include/llvm/codegen/selectiondag-h">SelectionDAG.h</a>, definition at line 4742 of file <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/lib/lib/codegen/lib/codegen/selectiondag/selectiondag-cpp">SelectionDAG.cpp</a>.</p>

### ComputeNumSignBits() {#aa0007d0a081ae03902143cb1f001afbb}

<div class="doxyMemberItem">
<div class="doxyMemberProto">
<table class="doxyMemberLabels">
<tr class="doxyMemberLabels">
<td class="doxyMemberLabelsLeft">
<table class="doxyMemberName">
<tr>
<td class="doxyMemberName">unsigned SelectionDAG::ComputeNumSignBits (<a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/sdvalue">SDValue</a> Op, <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/lib/lib/target/lib/target/aarch64/aarch64promoteconstant-cpp/#a90f8350fecae261c25be85d38b451bff">const</a> <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/apint">APInt</a> &amp; DemandedElts, unsigned Depth=0)</td>
</tr>
</table>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Return the number of times the sign bit of the register is replicated into the other bits.</p>


<p>We know that at least 1 bit is always equal to the sign bit (itself), but other cases can give us information. For example, immediately after an "SRA X, 2", we know that the top 3 bits are all equal to each other, so we return 3. The DemandedElts argument allows us to only collect the minimum sign bits of the requested vector elements. Targets can implement the ComputeNumSignBitsForTarget method in the <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/targetlowering">TargetLowering</a> class to allow target nodes to be understood.</p>


<p>Declaration at line 2066 of file <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/include/include/llvm/include/llvm/codegen/selectiondag-h">SelectionDAG.h</a>, definition at line 4754 of file <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/lib/lib/codegen/lib/codegen/selectiondag/selectiondag-cpp">SelectionDAG.cpp</a>.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Loads are not normal binary operators: their result type is not determined by their operands, and they produce a value AND a token chain.</p>


<p>This function will set the MOLoad flag on MMOFlags, but you can set it if you want. The MOStore flag must not be set.</p>

<p>These are used for target selectors to create a new node with specified return type(s), <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/machineinstr">MachineInstr</a> opcode, and operands.</p>


<p>getMachineNode - These are used for target selectors to create a new node with specified return type(s), <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/machineinstr">MachineInstr</a> opcode, and operands.</p>


<p>Note that getMachineNode returns the resultant node. If there is already a node of the specified opcode and operands, it returns that node instead of the current one.</p>

<p>Compute a TokenFactor to force all the incoming stack arguments to be loaded from the stack.</p>


<p>getStackArgumentTokenFactor - Compute a TokenFactor to force all the incoming stack arguments to be loaded from the stack.</p>


<p>This is used in tail call lowering to protect stack arguments from being clobbered.</p>

</tr>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Test whether <span class="doxyComputerOutput">V</span> has a splatted value for all the demanded elements.</p>


<p>isSplatValue - Return true if the vector V has the same value across all DemandedElts.</p>


<p>On success <span class="doxyComputerOutput">UndefElts</span> will indicate the elements that have UNDEF values instead of the splat value, this is only guaranteed to be correct for <span class="doxyComputerOutput">DemandedElts</span>.</p>


<p>NOTE: The function will return true for a demanded splat of UNDEF values.</p>


<p>For scalable vectors, we don't know the number of lanes at compile time. Instead, we use a 1 bit <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/apint">APInt</a> to represent a conservative value for all lanes; that is, that one bit value is implicitly splatted across all lanes.</p>

### LegalizeOp() {#a74ce53f838a5372200a8e8ec9b135316}

<div class="doxyMemberItem">
<div class="doxyMemberProto">
<table class="doxyMemberLabels">
<tr class="doxyMemberLabels">

<td class="doxyMemberName">bool SelectionDAG::LegalizeOp (<a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/sdnode">SDNode</a> * N, <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/smallsetvector">SmallSetVector</a>&lt; <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/sdnode">SDNode</a> *, 16 &gt; &amp; UpdatedNodes)</td>
</tr>
</table>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Transforms a <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/selectiondag">SelectionDAG</a> node and any operands to it into a node that is compatible with the target instruction selector, as indicated by the <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/targetlowering">TargetLowering</a> object.</p>


<dl class="doxySectionUser">
<dt>Returns</dt>
<dd><p>true if <span class="doxyComputerOutput">N</span> is a valid, legal node after calling this.</p></dd>
</dl>


<p>This essentially runs a single recursive walk of the <span class="doxyComputerOutput">Legalize</span> process over the given node (and its operands). This can be used to incrementally legalize the DAG. All of the nodes which are directly replaced, potentially including N, are added to the output parameter <span class="doxyComputerOutput">UpdatedNodes</span> so that the delta to the DAG can be understood by the caller.</p>


<p>When this returns false, N has been legalized in a way that make the pointer passed in no longer valid. It may have even been deleted from the DAG, and so it shouldn't be used further. When this returns true, the N passed in is a legal node, and can be immediately processed as such. This may still have done some work on the DAG, and will still populate UpdatedNodes with any new nodes replacing those originally in the DAG.</p>


<p>Declaration at line 643 of file <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/include/include/llvm/include/llvm/codegen/selectiondag-h">SelectionDAG.h</a>, definition at line 5857 of file <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/lib/lib/codegen/lib/codegen/selectiondag/legalizedag-cpp">LegalizeDAG.cpp</a>.</p>


<p>References <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/smallptrsetimpl/#a1f475b0df44ebd7169e720fa1bf9169e">llvm::SmallPtrSetImpl&lt; PtrType &gt;::count</a>, <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/smallptrsetimpl/#a9d834ae3da8c62c2b668dada51335eb0">llvm::SmallPtrSetImpl&lt; PtrType &gt;::insert</a> and <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/files/lib/lib/support/regcomp-c/#a0240ac851181b84ac374872dc5434ee4">N</a>.</p>

<p>MaskedValueIsZero - Return true if 'V &amp; Mask' is known to be zero in DemandedElts.</p>


<p>We use this predicate to simplify operations downstream. <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/namespaces/llvm/#ab471937b9a227e70c7fe8bd9604014d6">Op</a> and Mask are known to be the same type.</p>


<p>We use this predicate to simplify operations downstream. Mask is known to be zero for bits that V cannot have.</p>

### MorphNodeTo() {#a5877bd47049087f890aed4f0f501ec3f}

<div class="doxyMemberItem">
<div class="doxyMemberProto">

</tr>
</table>
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>This <em>mutates</em> the specified node to have the specified return type, opcode, and operands.</p>


<p>MorphNodeTo - This <em>mutates</em> the specified node to have the specified return type, opcode, and operands.</p>


<p>Note that MorphNodeTo returns the resultant node. If there is already a node of the specified opcode and operands, it returns that node instead of the current one. Note that the <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/sdloc">SDLoc</a> need not be the same.</p>


<p>Using MorphNodeTo is faster than creating a new node and swapping it in with ReplaceAllUsesWith both because it often avoids allocating a new node, and because it doesn't require CSE recalculation for any of the node's users.</p>


<p>However, note that MorphNodeTo recursively deletes dead nodes from the DAG. As a consequence it isn't appropriate to use from within the DAG combiner or the legalizer which maintain worklists that would need to be updated when deleting things.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Modify anything using 'From' to use 'To' instead.</p>


<p>ReplaceAllUsesWith - Modify anything using 'From' to use 'To' instead.</p>


<p>This can cause recursive merging of nodes in the DAG. <a href="/web-llvm/docs/api/classes/llvm/use">Use</a> the first version if 'From' is known to have a single result, use the second if you have two nodes with identical results (or if 'To' has a superset of the results of 'From'), use the third otherwise.</p>


<p>These methods all take an optional UpdateListener, which (if not null) is informed about nodes that are deleted and modified due to recursive changes in the dag.</p>


<p>These functions only replace all existing uses. It's possible that as these replacements are being performed, CSE may cause the From node to be given new uses. These new uses of From are left in place, and not automatically transferred to To.</p>


<p>This can cause recursive merging of nodes in the DAG.</p>


<p>This version assumes From has a single result value.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p>Utility function used by legalize and lowering to "unroll" a vector operation by splitting out the scalars and operating on each element individually.</p>


<p>If the ResNE is 0, fully unroll the vector op. If ResNE is less than the width of the vector op, unroll up to ResNE. If the ResNE is greater than the width of the vector op, unroll the vector op and fill the end of the resulting vector with UNDEFS.</p>

<div class="doxyMemberDoc">

<p><em>Mutate</em> the specified node in-place to have the specified operands.</p>


<p>UpdateNodeOperands - <em>Mutate</em> the specified node in-place to have the specified operands.</p>


<p>If the resultant node already exists in the DAG, this does not modify the specified node, instead it returns the node that already exists. If the resultant node does not exist in the DAG, the input node is returned. As a degenerate case, if you specify the same input operands as the node already has, the input node is returned.</p>
